DISTRICT DEVELOPMENT
STATISTICAL REPORT
Illustrative dataset for testing Report Navigator
Reporting year: 2024–25
Coverage: Five fictional districts in the fictional state of Dakshin Pradesh
Important notice
This document is entirely synthetic. All district names, population figures, literacy rates, employment estimates,
and other statistics are fictional and were created solely to test PDF extraction, table parsing, retrieval,
calculations, and page citations. They do not describe any real government, state, district, or population.
Suggested test questions
• What is the total population across the five districts?
• Which district has the highest literacy rate?
• Compare the female literacy rates of Nandipur and Suryanagar.
• What is the unemployment rate in each district?
• What was the change in school enrolment between 2023–24 and 2024–25?
• Is a district-level poverty rate provided?

SAMPLE DATASET — FICTIONAL / FOR SOFTWARE TESTING ONLY
PDF page 2
1. Executive Summary
This illustrative report presents selected development indicators for five fictional districts in Dakshin Pradesh. It is
designed to contain both narrative passages and structured statistical tables so that document-intelligence
systems can be tested against realistic report-like content.
Across the five districts, the combined estimated population is 5,000,000. Suryanagar records the highest literacy
rate at 92.1%, while Devgarh records the lowest at 78.4%. The report includes population, literacy, employment,
education, and health indicators.
The figures are point-in-time estimates for demonstration. They should not be interpreted as official statistics or
used for policy, research, or public decision-making.

5. Definitions, Methodology and Data Availability
Population: Fictional estimated number of usual residents in each district for the 2024–25 reporting period.
Literacy rate: Fictional percentage of the population classified as literate in the illustrative dataset. The report does
not specify an age threshold.
Labour force: Fictional number of persons included in the labour force estimate. Unemployment rate is calculated
as unemployed persons divided by labour force, multiplied by 100.
Enrolment change: Difference between the 2024–25 and 2023–24 student enrolment counts. Percentage change
is calculated relative to the 2023–24 count.
Data availability limitations
The following information is intentionally absent: district-level poverty rates, household income distribution,
migration flows, crop yields, road length, detailed age-group population, and district-level public expenditure. A
reliable question-answering system should report these as not found in this document rather than infer or fabricate
values.
Suggested evaluation prompts
1. What is the combined population of all five districts?
2. Which district has the highest total literacy rate?
3. What is the literacy-rate difference between Suryanagar and Devgarh?
4. Which district has the highest unemployment rate?
5. Calculate the percentage increase in enrolment in Kalyanpur.
6. Which district has the most health centres?
7. What is the poverty rate in Madhavgarh?
8. Does the report provide average household income?
End of illustrative report. All content and statistics are fictional.
